info.name: Healthcare Treatment Journey — Camunda 8.9
info.description:
End-to-end driver for the inpatient admission-to-discharge process.

## Setup

1. Import `healthcare-treatment-journey.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Fill in `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `clusterId`, `region` from Camunda Console.
3. Run **00 Auth → Get access token** once. Every other request reuses the cached token and the collection pre-request script refreshes it automatically ~60s before expiry.

## Running

Folders are ordered. `Runner` works on folders 02 and 03 top to bottom, but the process is asynchronous: Camunda needs a moment between a completion and the next task appearing. Each polling request retries itself via `setNextRequest`, so the Runner handles this without manual delays.

## Known blockers (verified 2026-07-29)

- **AI tasks incident** without an `OPENAI_API_KEY` connector secret in Camunda Console. `02.5 Skip AI history summary` routes around this via process-instance modification.
- **Vitals loop does not converge.** The framework IdempotencyGuard keys on job type + elementId + caseId, which are identical on every loop pass, so the second `vitals-monitoring` execution is treated as a replay and completed without running. `vitalsTrend` stays `DETERIORATING` and the discharge gate never opens. `02.9 Force discharge route` works around it.

request.description: RecordArchiveWorker writes one `patient_case` row keyed on caseId. Postman cannot query PostgreSQL, so the SQL to confirm it is logged to the console.
`diagnosticSystemDown` makes LabTestOrderWorker raise the BPMN error DIAGNOSTIC_SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE instead of returning an order.
The whole point of this folder: the worker throws a BPMN error, the boundary error event on the diagnostics sub-process catches it, and Escalate to Physician appears for `attending-physician`.
The escalation branch ends at ErrEnd_1 once completed. Cancelling instead keeps the cluster tidy when re-running the collection.
